question.worked_solution:
The given repeating decimal can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}0.0\overset{―}{28} & =0.028\,282\,8...… \\  & =0.028+0.000\,28+0.000\,002\,8+… \\  & ={{\frac{28}{1\,000}+\frac{28}{100\,000}+\frac{28}{10\,000\,000}+⋯.}_{⏟}}_{\text{geometric series}}\end{aligned}
$$

We see that we have a geometric series where the first term ${a}_{1}=\frac{28}{1\,000}$ and the common ratio is $r=\frac{1}{100}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}0.0\overset{―}{28} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{28}{1\,000}{(\frac{1}{100})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{28}{10}(\frac{1}{100}){(\frac{1}{100})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }2.8{(\frac{1}{100})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$
